top_strength: Excellent budget-conscious selling — after hearing that total cost was the whole reason for the call, she proactively volunteered that moving to a Monday-Thursday value day saves $36-45, then stacked the no-deposit and no-change-fee messaging on top. Her handling of the customer's confusion about whether the $200/hr was on top of the $980-1180 was clear, patient, and completely resolved it.
coaching_note: This call died at the close. Michelle was warm, agreed to everything, and Chauny even told her 'we do have two trucks left on this particular day' — a scarcity cue with no ask attached to it. She let the customer leave to 'finalize with the other party' without ever saying 'there's no deposit, let me hold that truck for you now and you can move or cancel it for free once you confirm.' Every ingredient for that ask was already on the table. Pair that with a real close sequence: book attempt, then 'reply to the email with any corrections,' then hours and callback number, then 'any other questions before I let you go?' She scored 3/11 on Quote/Booking on a call she had genuinely earned.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm and reassuring with a nervous, unsure customer — 'You're okay, you're okay, not a problem at all, I got you covered' and the 'Google is our cousin' line — and the customer reciprocated with 'awesome', 'oh nice', and 'sounds good', though name use was minimal.
audio_review_reason: Call opened with an audio failure (customer asking 'can you hear me?') and the transcript is garbled in several stretches; worth an ear to confirm line quality and that the warmth reads the same in voice.
